problem.headingLead: Four things that cost you money
problem.subhead: We hear all four from Texas managers. Each one costs money before anyone sees it.

calls.title: The 10 pm call
calls.body: A tenant calls about a leak after hours, in Spanish. Nobody answers, so the leak becomes a ceiling.
calls.cost: A leak left until morning can become a turn: $1,500 to $8,000 a unit

payments.title: "I already paid"
payments.body: Cash, money orders, Zelle and checks arrive five different ways. Matching them eats a day every month.
payments.cost: A day a month of matching is about $4,200 a year in staff time

deadlines.title: The forgotten clock
deadlines.body: Deposits are due 30 days after the forwarding address. Health and safety repairs, 7 days after notice.
deadlines.cost: Bad-faith deposit retention can cost $100 plus three times the deposit (§92.109)

switching.title: Stuck where you are
switching.body: Your tenants can't read the portal, and switching means weeks of data entry nobody has time for.

ai.eyebrow: Done for you · set up by our team
ai.subhead: Our team sets up and runs an after-hours bilingual service for your company: the phone line, maintenance intake, missed-call text-back and late-fee reminders. It is included in the monthly price.

voice.title: After-hours bilingual phone line
voice.body: An AI line our team sets up answers tenant calls after hours in English or Spanish and logs each request for your staff.

intake.title: After-hours maintenance intake
intake.body: Repair calls at night are taken down with the unit and the details, ready for your staff in the morning.

textback.title: Missed-call text-back
textback.body: Every call your office misses gets a text back in the caller's language, so nobody is left waiting.

reminders.title: Reminders before a late fee is chargeable
reminders.body: Tenants hear from you before a late fee can be charged. Fewer late payments, fewer arguments.

ai.guardrail: The line never changes a balance, waives a fee or sends a legal notice. It hands those to your staff.

features.subhead: Six things the software does. Not adjectives - the actual actions your staff take and your tenants see.

portal.title: A portal tenants can read
portal.body: Every screen in English and Spanish, translated key by key. Not a translate widget bolted onto an English app.

queue.title: Every request in one queue
queue.body: Portal, phone or walk-in, with the source recorded by your staff, so nothing falls through whichever way the tenant reached you.

payments.title: Every way tenants pay
payments.body: Card, ACH and cash through PayNearMe in the portal. Tenants who pay by Zelle or check report it with a photo, and staff confirm it against the bank.

maintenance.title: Maintenance with photos
maintenance.body: Requests carry images from the tenant's phone, get assigned to a vendor, and are tracked through to close.

compliance.title: Texas deadlines in the form
compliance.body: Late-fee limits, the deposit clock, the repair window and rekey deadlines are tracked against the dates the statute counts from.

cycle.title: The month's rent in one pass
cycle.body: Generate every invoice for the period, review the batch before it goes out, and send them together.

proof.subhead: No testimonials or logos on this page. Here is what you can check on the walkthrough.

items.isolation: A test suite proves one company cannot read another's data

bilingual.headingLead: The leak gets reported while it is
bilingual.body: Both portals ship in English and Mexican Spanish - every screen, at exact parity, translated key by key rather than machine-translated at runtime.
bilingual.argument: This is not a courtesy feature. A tenant who cannot comfortably report a problem tends not to report it, and a small repair left alone stops being a small repair. Reading the request is the cheapest part of fixing it.
bilingual.parityLabel: translated strings, both portals, exact parity
bilingual.imageAlt: The same {{brand}} tenant portal screen side by side in English and Spanish

compliance.subhead: {{brand}} tracks these dates and warns you before they pass. It does not file anything for you.

lateFee.title: Late fees, held and capped
lateFee.body: The action stays disabled until rent is two full days late, and the amount is checked against the statutory cap.

deposit.title: The 30-day deposit clock
deposit.body: Starts when the forwarding address arrives, not at move-out, and tracks the itemised disposition against it.

repair.title: The seven-day repair window
repair.body: Conditions affecting health or safety carry a day counter from the tenant's written notice, amber before it lapses and red after.

rekey.title: Rekey within seven days
rekey.body: A new tenancy opens a turnover checklist with the rekey deadline counted from the day possession starts.

notice.title: Notice to vacate
notice.body: Generated as a PDF and recorded against the lease, with the date it was delivered.

reminders.title: Reminders before a late fee is chargeable
reminders.body: Tenants hear from you before a late fee can be charged. Fewer late payments, fewer arguments.

guarantee.title: The 30-day guarantee
guarantee.body: Your portfolio is live and your first rent cycle runs in Rentio within 30 days of us receiving your data export, or your first invoice waits until it does. We do the migration, so this is on us.
guarantee.exit: After the first 6 months, leave any month. We export every unit, tenant, lease and payment for you within 2 business days.

switching.q: We're on AppFolio or Buildium. How painful is switching?
switching.a: Not on your side. We import your units, tenants and leases from your export and train your staff in one session. Most companies are live in 3–5 business days, and if your first rent cycle isn't running in Rentio within 30 days of your export, your first invoice waits.

fees.q: Do my tenants pay a fee to pay rent?
fees.a: No portal fees for tenants from us, ever. They can pay by card, ACH or cash through PayNearMe, or keep paying by Zelle or money order and report it in the portal with a photo.

ai.a: Yes. Our team sets up your after-hours line in English and Spanish during onboarding. It logs requests for your staff; it never changes a balance, waives a fee or sends a legal notice.

spanish.a: No. Every screen is in English and Mexican Spanish and each person picks their own.

texas.q: Does it keep me compliant with Texas law?
texas.a: It tracks the §92 deadlines and the late-fee cap inside the forms and warns you before they pass. It is not legal advice.

data.q: Who owns the data, and can I leave?
data.a: You do. After the first 6 months, leave any month; we export every unit, tenant, lease and payment for you within 2 business days.

doors.q: How many doors do I need?
doors.a: Rentio is built for 50–500 doors; best fit 80–500. The price is the same {{monthlyPrice}} a month at any size. Under 50 doors, we'll tell you on the call that TurboTenant is the cheaper fit.

cost.a: {{monthlyPrice}} a month for the software, the AI night shift set up by our team, and a named person. {{setupFee}} once for migration, training and your website. No per-door fees, no tenant portal fees.

setupFee.q: Why is there a setup fee?
setupFee.a: The {{setupFee}} covers the work we do for you once: moving your data over, configuring Rentio and your AI line for your company, and training your staff.

hiddenFees.q: Are there hidden fees for payments, screening or e-sign?
hiddenFees.a: No. We don't charge a single extra dollar on top of {{monthlyPrice}} a month. No per-door fees, no per-payment fees, no add-ons.

contract.q: What's the contract length? Can I cancel?
contract.a: The minimum is 6 months. After that, cancel any time.

live.a: 3–5 business days for most companies, counted from when we receive your data export.

migration.q: Who does the migration, you or us?
migration.a: Us. You send the export; we move everything over and check it with you.

staff.a: No. It frees up your staff, it doesn't fire them. The AI takes the repetitive calls and messages so your team spends its time on the work that needs a person.

afterHours.q: Does it handle after-hours emergency maintenance calls?
afterHours.a: Yes, in English and Spanish. The AI line answers at night and on weekends and logs every request for your staff.

money.q: Does it do trust accounting and owner statements?
money.a: Yes. Every dollar coming in and going out is recorded and can be traced, and owner statements are created under Reports, by property or unit, ready to send.

tenantPortal.q: Is there a tenant portal for rent and maintenance?
tenantPortal.a: Yes. Tenants report their rent payments and submit maintenance requests with photos in the portal, in English or Spanish.

payMethods.q: Can tenants pay by card, ACH or cash?
payMethods.a: Yes. Card and ACH in the tenant portal, and cash at a nearby store through PayNearMe. Each payment lands in the ledger on its own.

ownerPortal.q: Can owners log in and see their reports?
ownerPortal.a: Yes. Each owner gets a login to see earnings, cash in and cash out, the balance sheet, what they owe and what is owed to them. If they want, they can connect more of their business to see it all in one place.

quickbooks.a: Yes. Payments and expenses flow into your QuickBooks, so your books and Rentio always agree.

prep.headingLead: Three things that make the call
prep.subhead: Each one takes under two minutes. Together they turn a demo into a walkthrough of your own portfolio.

watch.title: Watch the video above
watch.body: It tells you what we will and won't do on the call, so there are no surprises.

reply.title: Reply to your confirmation email
reply.body: Two lines: how many doors you manage, and what software you use today. We load a few of your units ahead of time so you see your own rent roll, not a demo account.

invite.title: Bring the person who runs your office
invite.body: The one who answers the tenant calls and matches the payments. They will have the questions that matter, and they are the one the switch has to work for.

agenda.subhead: Here is the whole call, minute by minute, so you know what you are walking into.

portfolio.title: Your portfolio, in Rentio
portfolio.body: A few of your units and leases, already loaded. You see your rent roll, your work orders and what your tenants would see on their phone, in Spanish.

moments.title: The three moments
moments.body: A tenant reports a Zelle payment with a screenshot. A deposit clock already running on a move-out. A leak reported at 10 pm that is a work order with photos by morning.

plan.title: The number and the plan
plan.body: Your price, what your 30 days look like, and whether it is a fit. If it isn't, we will say so and you have lost half an hour.

day.subhead: Nothing here is invented. These are the four calls and questions every Texas manager told us about.

morning.before: Three voicemails in Spanish from last night. One of them is a leak. Nobody is sure which.
morning.after: The leak is a work order with two photos. The tenant filed it from the portal at 10:12 pm, in Spanish.

payment.before: A tenant insists they paid by Zelle on Friday. Someone spends an hour in the bank app.
payment.after: The Zelle payment is in the confirm queue with the tenant's screenshot. One click matches it.

deposit.before: Unit 204 moved out. When did the forwarding address arrive? When is the deposit due back?
deposit.after: Unit 204 shows 11 days left on the deposit clock, counted from the day the forwarding address came in.

night.before: Your personal phone rings. It's a tenant.
night.after: Tenants report problems in the portal, in their language. Your phone stays on the counter.

path.subhead: Switching software fails when the manager has to do the data entry. So we do it.

day0.title: The walkthrough

day30.label: Day 30

closing.body: Watch the video, reply with your door count and software, and bring the person who runs your office. Everything else is on us.
closing.reschedule: Can't make it? Reschedule from your confirmation email. A moved call is fine. A missed one wastes the prep we did on your portfolio.
